item.title: 11 Sep 2026 10:30
item.description:
The marines organized a stair climb event this morning to commemorate 9/11. Climbed 3 floors 38 times. They had their flaks on and one of them even had a gas mask on. I was breathing hard at the end of the 10th lap. Legs felt quite jelly by the 20th. Started sipping water from the 25th lap and finally finished reasonably good at the 38th. A good cold shower was all that was needed to feel normal. Oddly this felt a bit more challenging than last time.

I was around 15 when we got the news of the twin towers. Miss Bama was supposed to be landing in the U.S that day. We’d only hear a day later that her flight was routed to Canada and someone drove her over to where she had to get to.

25 years have passed and we’re still at it! Paying the 911 tax - $5.60 for every single flight ticket that you take on U.S soil. Any perceived victory in any war is all just a mirage. 🔗

item.title: 13 Jul 2024 13:49
item.description: The pains and joys of self-hosting and tinkering. There’s always something that is broken, ready to be fixed, to be upgraded, can be built upon or changed. It is like a puzzle that constantly evolves depending on the time you invest in it. And every once in a while it exposes the silver lining that keeps you hooked to it.

item.title: 21 Jun 2024 20:06
item.description: M and I tend to share photos with family and friends on various chat groups. While straightforward, It felt redundant to share copies of the same pictures in multiple places. I’ve been looking for options to share album links instead that would give us a bit more control. All our photos are primarily saved in a Nextcloud self-hosted instance. I explored a few options of album shares there but wasn’t quite happy. Pixelfed was another option I explored. It did check most of the requirements but I wasn’t quite comfortable relying on a software that’s mostly dependent on just one developer. Also the unlisted feature on their albums seemed half-baked and not yet ready for prime-time. Finally played a bit with PhotoPrism and so far it seems to be something that checks all the boxes. With private links, a PWA app and great thumbnails this might be the closest solution for my photo needs.

item.title: 08 Jun 2024 19:32
item.description:
Brought the Grand Vitara home today. We’d been on the lookout for a decent car ever since we knew about our next posting. We don’t need one here in CDMX but would definitely need one in Yaounde. All I wanted was a reliable bare minimum car with no gadgetry shabangs. Over the last few months folks on their PCS did post a few decent cars but these are barely in the market for a few hours. With this one though, the stars seemed to align all well one day and we were able to seal the deal in a few hours.

Given the mileage, the GV might need some maintenance over the next few years. It rides like butter now though and reminds me of the Grand Cherokee we had in NYC/BOS.
